page_title: Lockpaw: One key. Screen covered. Everything running.

sources.entry: Lockpaw - Menu bar screen guard for macOS — lock and unlock your screen with a hotkey. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/sorkila/lockpaw) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Lockpaw
summary.one_liner: Lockpaw is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that locks your screen with a hotkey while keeping the Mac awake so AI agents, builds and downloads keep running.
use_cases: Lock a Mac while long builds or downloads keep running
Step away while AI coding agents work and get alerted when they need input
Keep agents running with the laptop lid closed while the screen is locked
Lock the screen quickly from a keyboard shortcut, Shortcuts, Spotlight or Siri
Get phone notifications when a coding agent needs permission
summary.what_it_does: ["Locks the Mac screen with a hotkey (⌘⇧L) or from Shortcuts, Spotlight or Siri, without putting the Mac to sleep, so processes, SSH sessions and downloads continue.", "Shows a covered screen that glows when a supported AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot CLI or Aider) needs attention, with a notification naming the agent and reason; alerts are silent by default.", "Offers an optional helper, enabled from Login Items, that keeps the Mac awake with the lid closed while locked; sleep returns on unlock, when the Mac runs hot, or at 20% battery.", "Unlocks with Touch ID or password, and lets you choose a dog, cat, your own image, or no mascot; can dim to black for OLED screens without sleeping the display."]
notable: Keeps AI agents, builds and downloads running while the screen is locked, unlike sleep-based approaches
Agent alerts for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot CLI and Aider, with optional push to phone via ntfy, Pushover or webhook
About 14 MB native Swift app with no analytics or accounts; installable via Homebrew cask
caveats: The page's own FAQ asks whether Lockpaw is a real security lock; the page text does not give a clear answer beyond describing it as a screen guard, so treat it as not verified for security use.
The lid-closed stay-awake feature is optional and only active while the screen is locked; the helper must be allowed once in Login Items.
